Definition: to pawn; causatively, to lend (on security); figuratively, to entangle
BiblicalUsage: This verb for lending on pledge — to take security, to lend — turns up in Moses' promises to Israel: 'thou shalt lend unto many nations, but thou shalt not borrow' is both the blessing of obedience in Deuteronomy 15:6 and of Deuteronomy 28:12. Lending marks the nation that has enough to give; borrowing marks the nation in want.
TheologicalSignificance: It is an economic word, but the promise behind it is spiritual: obedience would make Israel the lender, not the borrower. I believe God still ties provision to obedience — not as a bargain, but as a pattern — and a people who trust Him end up with enough to share.
